implication: First-token quality failure is concentrated at a narrow top-2 boundary rather than random-token corruption.

evidence: All four variants have nonzero top-k rank changes on all three payloads.
implication: Even variants with stable selected token still perturb the top-k ordering.

evidence: Case 2 has top-k membership drift for every tested variant; cases 0/1 are variant-specific.
implication: Case 2 is the strongest common regression payload and remains the best targeted diagnostic payload.

evidence: HQQ6 g32 removes selected-token flips but worsens aggregate top-k deltas versus g64; HQQ6 g16 and HQQ8 g64 are worse on aggregate and/or selected-token stability.
implication: More HQQ bit/group sweeps are not justified from this data; quality does not improve monotonically with smaller groups or higher nbits.
